segmentation.text: Where the signal is a flashing yellow turn arrow, displayed alone or in combination with another signal:
enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal,
or other such movement as is permitted by other signal indications displayed at the same time.
to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk
to other traffic lawfully within the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., flashing_yellow_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a flashing yellow turn arrow is flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn, with whatever other states the head displays ('alone or in combination with another signal').

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).
'Such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s11 reads. As the index maps 'must yield' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'other traffic': road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') other than the subject. 'within the intersection': its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection). As the index maps 'lawfully using the intersection.' (NRS_484B_307_4a_o2).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, faces traffic signal head s showing a flashing yellow turn arrow: either it occupies a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which s governs (dev.governs), and s displays flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn (with or without other states) at the judged observation; or it occupies i, has occupied it at every observation since it entered i from such a c, and s displayed such an arrow at that entry.
obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class traffic and whose footprint overlaps i at the judged observation: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within the intersection' is read through the other road user's presence within the intersection; whether its presence there is lawful is not judged, so the subject yields to every such road user.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Head s governing left-turn lane c displays circular_green with flashing_yellow_arrow(left); an oncoming car already inside i proceeds straight at 11 m/s; the car turns left across its path at 6 m/s, the closest approach of their centres 0.9 s ahead at 1.2 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same signal; no other road user is in the scene; the car turns left through i. The duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays green_arrow(left) alone; the car turns left past an oncoming car.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no velocity-derived speed for the turning car: whether it moved on toward the oncoming car is unknown.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged
